title: Torrance
name: Torrance
metaDescription: Torrance 1031 exchange advisory for owners trading South Bay industrial flex space, Del Amo-area retail pads, and workforce apartments near Torrance's job centers.

sections.html: Torrance sits a few miles inland from the harbor, and its commercial base splits fairly evenly among industrial and flex buildings tied to a long aerospace and manufacturing history, retail centered on the Del Amo corridor, and apartment buildings that house the workforce filling those buildings each morning. A Torrance seller is rarely trading one asset type in isolation, since the owner of a flex building near the airport often holds a nearby apartment property as well, and both sides of that portfolio need their own replacement search. Torrance's price levels sit below Westside and Beverly Hills comparables, which keeps the city attractive to buyers priced out of those corridors but still targeting Los Angeles County industrial and multifamily fundamentals.

sections.heading: What Actually Trades in Torrance's Industrial and Flex Stock
sections.html:
Torrance's industrial buildings trace back to decades of aerospace subcontracting and automotive-parts manufacturing, and much of that stock sits on lots too small and too oddly configured for a modern logistics user, which keeps older owner-users and small manufacturers in place rather than pushing turnover toward big-box tenants. Flex space near Zamperini Field at Torrance Municipal Airport adds a second layer, mixing light assembly, office showroom, and small aviation-support tenants on the same block.

Multifamily in Torrance skews toward two- and three-story garden buildings built in the 1960s through 1980s, with newer construction concentrated closer to the Del Amo retail corridor. Retail itself ranges from the enclosed mall anchor down to single-tenant pads along Hawthorne Boulevard, and an owner selling one of those pads is usually comparing it against a narrower set of net-lease alternatives than a mall-adjacent investor would consider.

sections.heading: Identification Choices Around the Del Amo Corridor
sections.html:
An owner exchanging out of a single Hawthorne Boulevard retail pad can often stay inside the three-property rule if the replacement search stays within net-lease retail. Someone exiting an aerospace-era industrial building and open to a broader replacement list typically needs more room, since the categories worth comparing in Torrance span:

  • Small-bay industrial and flex buildings near the airport
  • Single-tenant retail pads along Hawthorne Boulevard
  • Garden-style apartment buildings built before 1990
  • Owner-user manufacturing buildings on legacy aerospace-adjacent lots
  • DST interests for owners exiting active property management

sections.heading: How Lenders Read Torrance Industrial and Apartment Product
sections.html:
Lenders tend to like Torrance industrial because so little new supply has been built in the South Bay in recent years, and older buildings on small lots are effectively impossible to replicate given how built-out the surrounding blocks already are. That scarcity supports value, but it also means an appraiser has fewer true comparables to draw on, and a buyer should expect that gap to show up as a wider range in the appraisal rather than a single clean number.

On the apartment side, California's statewide rent cap under AB 1482 applies to most buildings that are not otherwise exempt, and a lender underwriting a Torrance property will want to see how that cap interacts with current rents before finalizing terms. An owner should confirm exemption status for any building older stock qualifies under rather than assuming the statewide cap does not apply.

sections.heading: Where Torrance Diligence Gets Missed
sections.html: Torrance is still home to petroleum refining and decades of industrial manufacturing, and a buyer looking at an older industrial parcel should order a Phase I environmental review even when the current use looks clean, since prior tenants on legacy aerospace or manufacturing sites can leave soil or groundwater issues that only a proper report will surface. Flex buildings near the airport should also get a use and height check against airport-influence zoning before a lender will commit, and that review should start the same week the property is identified rather than after the qualified intermediary sets a closing date. Skipping either step is the fastest way to lose weeks an investor does not have inside the 180-day window.

sections.heading: Budgeting the Full Cost of a Torrance Replacement Purchase
sections.html:
An owner building a numbers-first budget for a Torrance replacement should carry three line items beyond the purchase price: the Phase I environmental cost on older industrial buildings, a lender-required capital reserve for any apartment property with deferred maintenance from decades of ownership, and title and escrow fees that run higher on leasehold or ground-lease adjacent parcels near the airport. Underestimating any one of those three is the most common way a Torrance closing slips past its scheduled date.

Lifecycle cost also deserves attention on older flex and manufacturing buildings, since roof, HVAC, and electrical systems installed decades ago during the city's aerospace-era build-out are closer to replacement than a fresh coat of paint on the exterior might suggest. Pricing that remaining useful life into the offer, rather than treating the building as turnkey because it is occupied, keeps the post-closing budget realistic.

faqs.q: Why does Torrance's industrial history matter for a 1031 replacement search there?
faqs.a: Decades of aerospace and manufacturing use mean some older parcels carry environmental history that is not visible from a site visit. A Phase I environmental review is worth ordering early, even on a building that looks clean today, so any issue surfaces before the identification window closes rather than after.

faqs.q: Does California's AB 1482 rent cap apply to an apartment building I am buying in Torrance?
faqs.a: It applies to most multifamily buildings that are not otherwise exempt, regardless of whether the city has its own local ordinance. An owner should confirm the exemption status of the specific building rather than assume the statewide cap does or does not apply based on the building's age alone.

faqs.q: Will Torrance's tight industrial supply make my replacement search faster?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Scarcity supports pricing, but it also means fewer directly comparable buildings for an appraiser to draw on, which can widen the appraisal range and slow lender sign-off. An owner casting a broader net across flex, small-bay industrial, and owner-user product may need the 200 percent rule rather than relying on three close comparables.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Los Angeles confirm my Torrance property qualifies for an exchange?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates planning, property identification, and communication among an investor's advisors. Whether a specific transaction and property qualify is a determination made by the investor's CPA, tax attorney, and qualified intermediary.
